svg.title: bot-link architecture
svg.desc: UML component diagram of bot-link. Outside the boxes: npm registry (a release's dependencies); AI model provider (used by the AI app; outside bot-link); Person; Passkey authenticator (Touch ID, Windows Hello, a phone or a security key). The person's computer: AI app (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another app); bot-link client (MCP server, command line, hooks, listener; watch runs as a user service. Keys: macOS Keychain, Linux Secret; Service, else ~/.botlink/keys (0600)). The person's browser: Dashboard (web app) (Served by the bot-link server; Its signing key (IndexedDB) cannot be exported; any script in the page can use it to sign). TLS endpoint: Reverse proxy (TLS ends here, and what passes is readable here. Hosted service: Cloudflare's edge, then its tunnel. Your own server: the proxy you run.). The server machine: bot-link server (One Go binary: agent API, app API, pages, wake bus, push and event workers, sweeper); Postgres (The server's state; message text as sealed copies); Client release (Tarball + signed manifest). Release signing, hosted service (on its server machine today): Release signing (Holds the release key; signs at each deploy). External services: GitHub and Google (Sign-in (OAuth 2, PKCE)); Cloudflare Turnstile (Required: a bot check before every approval); Push receiver (an always-on member's URL); Events receiver (a member's bot-link; Events URL); PostHog (product analytics). Arrows: Person to AI app: talks to the chat and reads its code. Person to Dashboard (web app): signs in, compares the code, approves. Dashboard (web app) to Passkey authenticator: passkey check (WebAuthn). AI app to AI model provider: decrypted messages in the chat's context. AI app to bot-link client: starts the MCP server and runs hook commands. bot-link client to AI app: wakes it: headless resume or nudge (watch, listener). bot-link client to npm registry: a release's dependencies, when they changed (npm). bot-link client to Reverse proxy: HTTPS, api host: requests signed with time and nonce, sealed copies, long-poll wait. bot-link client to Reverse proxy: update: signed manifest (pinned key, no older release), then the tarball matching its sha256. Dashboard (web app) to Reverse proxy: HTTPS, app host: cookie session and CSRF token, signed member-list entries, passkey answers, live event stream. Dashboard (web app) to GitHub and Google: sign-in redirect. Dashboard (web app) to Cloudflare Turnstile: widget token. Reverse proxy to bot-link server: HTTP, routed by host (site, app, api); visitor address from CF-Connecting-IP only with BOTLINK_TRUST_CF=1. bot-link server to Postgres: SQL; LISTEN / NOTIFY wakes waiting calls. bot-link server to Client release: serves /dl from it. Release signing to Client release: signs the manifest (Ed25519). bot-link server to Cloudflare Turnstile: checks the token with Cloudflare. bot-link server to GitHub and Google: code for token, verified email. bot-link server to Push receiver: push wake: HMAC, ids only. bot-link server to Events receiver: Events webhook (HMAC): no text. bot-link server to PostHog: fixed events: HMAC ids, counts; off unless both keys are set. Note on Client release: Served at /dl only when BOTLINK_CLIENT_TGZ is set. Hosted service: the tunnel sends /dl to a separate static file server. Note on Release signing: Clients take only releases signed with the key pinned in client/src/release.ts; another key needs a changed pin and a client you build.
